body: You will probably have to make a (negative?) lookbehind in the regex when the end is reached to exclude the dot as inside the string itself it is valid.
I think the last char to inform to regexp to end of url is space or html tag, like this: https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/3392#issuecomment-45312089
I can take a look at this.

I took a look at this, and given that our autolinker is meant as a basic text linker and uses basic regular expressions, I don't think this is solvable. It seems that [several markdown](http://johnmacfarlane.net/babelmark2/?text=My+website+http%3A%2F%2Fexample.com.) parsers handle linking in the same way as we do.

Hi Markstory, the example link you provided in your example is rendered correctly by cake.
when the domain name has no parameters, the . is excluded from the link.

When you take this example "My website https://github.com/google/physical-web." 

I see that 3 of the 5 scripts make a link of it, en they make the link correctly:

"http://johnmacfarlane.net/babelmark2/?text=My+website+https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fgoogle%2Fphysical-web."

Also github excludes the dot in this URL.

But cake includes the dot in the URL.

> Also github excludes the dot in this URL.

Not consistently it doesn't:
-  https://github.com/google/physical-web.
- "https://github.com/google/physical-web."

In case things change, a screenshot from your last comment:

![screen shot 2014-12-05 at 09 44 52](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/33387/5313020/6610c832-7c63-11e4-8897-e57ea20f34a4.png)

Which probably simply indicates the awkwardness of trying to fix "the problem".

The markdown implementations that _do_ get it right seem to parse text one character at a time. This is not an implementation approach that fits the goals of TextHelper. If you need more powerful autolinking you might want to explore using a markdown parser or other text markup language and use an implementation that fits your needs.
@markstory Thank you for your response. I will then find a markdown parser to use.
@rayflexcom while it's for 3.x, [here is a tutorial](http://josediazgonzalez.com/2014/12/07/parsing-markdown-comments/) on writing a simple markdown helper.
